notes: All dates bucketed in UTC (Supabase session timezone). 110/124 real users have timezone='UTC', so local-day bucketing isn't possible anyway.

onto_projects/onto_tasks/onto_documents.created_by is an onto_actors id, not a user id; joined via onto_actors.user_id. 42 real users have no actor row at all (never touched the ontology product). 6 projects were created by actor kind='agent' (no user).
user_activity_logs is NOT a user activity source: 180 rows, all activity_type='admin_action'.
users.last_visit appears maintained: 33/124 real users have last_visit after signup day, 13 beyond 30 days. It only stores the latest visit, so it adds at most 1 extra active day per user.
chat_turn_runs only exists since 2026-04-04 and chat_turn_events since 2026-10-12; chat_sessions/chat_messages (since 2025-10-28) are the long-run chat source.
Document activation is inflated: document.context.project (142 rows, 40 creators) is auto-created with each project, so 'has document' ~= 'has project'.

Daily brief email counts agree across three paths (emails+email_recipients category=daily_brief: 6; email_logs subject: 5; notification_deliveries email+brief.completed: 6). Some older 'BuildOS Daily Brief - <Day>' emails sit under emails.category='notification', so the 'ever' figure (10) undercounts pre-2026-07 history.
2,793 email_recipients rows from one batch on 2025-10-13 ('Your Daily Brief is Ready!') are still status='pending' - a stuck/abandoned batch, never sent.

Monetization tables are empty: customer_subscriptions, invoices, payment_methods, failed_payments, trial_reminders all 0 rows. Nobody has ever paid. 121/123 real trials expired with no reminders ever sent.

Acquisition attribution is essentially absent: utm_* 0/127, signup_source 7/124, referrer 3/124. onboarding_project_id never set (0/127). users.preferences empty for all; productivity_challenges empty for 126/127.
Onboarding completion collapsed in 2026: 30/124 real users overall but only 6/52 of 2026 signups and 1/16 of last-90-day signups have onboarding_completed_at.

Project creation 'source' is not tracked on onto_projects (props.source only on 3 calendar_analysis projects). chat_sessions.context_type='project_create' sessions (24 from 14 real users) do not link to any created project via entity_id. onto_project_logs change_source (api/agent_call/chat/form) is the only creation-channel signal and only since 2026-01-04.
Legacy 'projects'/'tasks' tables (64/650 rows, 2025-05 to 2025-11) are the pre-ontology product; 21 real users only ever used that.
Project categorization (section 9) was done by reading titles/descriptions; counts only, no titles or identities retained in this file.

CORRECTION (ad-wave follow-up): two backfill days were counted as user activity in the first pass. 2025-12-17 (ontology migration created onto_projects/onto_tasks for 21 real users) and 2026-06-24 (document.context.project backfill for 22 real users). Sections 3 and 4 now exclude them; raw values kept under raw_before_backfill_exclusion. Real users with >=3 active days across >=2 weeks: 26 -> 11; >=2 active days: 44 -> 38; active 30+ days after signup: 27 -> 13.

ad_wave.context: Founder reports the only real signup wave came from cheap Instagram/Facebook ads aimed at adults with ADHD. Data: real signups Jul-2025 25 + Aug-2025 20 = 45 (36% of all 124 real users ever). Waitlist burst 2025-07-15 to 2025-08-08.

2b_waitlist_wave_window_2025-07-09_to_20.note: referral_source understates the ads: 48 of 68 July rows chose 'Other'/blank, and several free-text answers reference 'the ad' or 'the Instagram post'. The whole Jul-9..Aug-8 burst should be read as the ad wave; FB/IG labels concentrate 07-24..08-08.

notes: Waitlist (beta_signups) 87 rows: 68 in Jul-2025, 14 in Aug-2025, 5 later. 17 of the 81 wave-window rows match a real user email (21%); 45 real signups happened in those months, so most wave signups bypassed the waitlist or used a different email.
FB/IG-labelled waitlist matches (5 users): 1 made a project, max 2 active days, last activity 2025-08-15, none active since.

Wave-month cohort (45) vs post-wave (77): week-1 return 15/45 (33%) vs 7/77 (9%); onboarding completed 16/45 (36%) vs 12/77 (16%); >=3 active days 4/45 (9%) vs 6/77 (8%); active in last 90d 1/45 vs 19/77 (recency). The wave retained better in week 1 but equally poorly beyond.
0 of 45 wave users ever used chat: agentic chat shipped 2025-10-28, after the wave had churned. They only ever saw the legacy projects/tasks product.

Backfill exclusion applied: 2025-12-17 (onto project/task migration, 21 real users) and 2026-06-24 (document.context.project backfill, 22 real users) no longer count as activity anywhere in this file.
Free-text bucketing was done by reading each row; counts only, no quotes or identities retained.

1_fields.verdict: YES = default-checked opt-out box at every layer (form, API, DB). 74/87 rows carry the untouched true/true pair, including the single all-blank submission. The only deliberate signal is the 8 who unchecked community (12 unchecked calls, 7 unchecked both). 'Wanted community' should be read as 'did not opt out'.
1_fields.beta_members_mirror: beta_members (85 rows) copies the two flags and adds wants_feature_updates = true for 85/85; calls_attended, feedback_submitted and last_active_at are 0/never set for everyone.

community_wanters.2c_bucket_notes: working_on inferred from why_interested + job title (the waitlist has no 'what are you working on' field); founder/owner titles with no stated project are counted as business_clients. school_research and job_career had 0 waitlist rows. Team test row excluded (86 rows).

4_contactability.caveat: No unsubscribe/bounce store is populated (email_suppressions has 0 rows in the whole DB; emails carry unsubscribe links but nothing records a click-through), so 'not unsubscribed' is unproven. Open tracking shows 0 opens on the 72 reactivation sends, which contradicts the 1 recorded click; treat open counts as unreliable.

5_themes.method: substring scan of waitlist biggest_challenge/why_interested (87 rows) and onboarding user_context fields (31 real users, team account excluded) for the requested terms, then each hit read in context; counts are distinct people
paraphrased_examples: Solo builder: is the only designer, tester and PM on every project, so everything stops when they get pulled away; says they need external pressure or someone to keep them accountable, and asks for a weekly 'what you said vs what you shipped' report.
Remote clinician: cannot stay on task without body doubling and is already organizing body-doubling rooms with work peers to manage executive-function issues.
Waitlister with a dev background: short on time but offers to help test and guide the product to take it further.
Waitlister: would love to help build something that actually works, rather than just use it.
Self-described most disorganized person they know: if this works, they will be the case study.
Side-project developer: reaches 80-90% and drifts to the next thing, keeps adding features instead of shipping an MVP to get user feedback.
Waitlister: biggest challenge is not having a team and the skills a team would bring.
Person building a company around a full-time job: wants help staying motivated to work evenings and weekends.
5_themes.reading: Nobody asked for a peer community in their own words. The community-adjacent asks are accountability, body doubling, feedback loops on shipped work, and offers to test/contribute (6 people). Five respondents are themselves building communities for others.

notes: Cross-tab compares 78 opt-in vs 8 opt-out rows; with the box pre-checked, differences mostly reflect who bothered to uncheck (opt-outs skew blank-title, designer/creative, focus-challenge, 'curious about AI').
Only 18 of 79 community-wanters ever became real users; 1 is still active (last activity 2026-09), 0 ever used chat, median 2 lifetime active days.
beta_members was populated for 85/87 waitlist rows with access_level 'full', tier 'founder', and never updated afterwards (0 calls attended, 0 feedback, last_active_at null).
